lines.text: Odysseus was forced to leave his wife and newborn son, to sail toward a war that would consume ten years of his life.
The Greeks surrounded Troy for a decade, but its walls never fell.
So Odysseus stopped trying to win with strength.
He built a giant wooden horse, hid his best men inside it, and ordered the army to disappear.
The Trojans believed the horse was a gift. They dragged it to their gates, celebrated their victory, and went to sleep.
That night, Odysseus opened the gates and let the Greek army inside.
Before sunrise, the men of Troy were slaughtered. Homes were destroyed, and even sacred temples were violated.
The Greeks had finally won, but the gods were watching them enter Troy.
They saw men who had crossed every sacred line.
Odysseus had built the perfect weapon: a lie, disguised as a gift.
He knew they had broken sacred law. Zeus's law. He knew that guilt would follow him forever.
And from that night, every mile home would become the price of the victory he was so proud of.
